thread:
jordan (docs): Hey team — opened a PR to merge several retention snippets into a single "playbook" for SOC2-facing docs. Goal: one source of truth for retention timelines + example scrub/redaction code. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4923 :wave:

emma (security): Thanks. Quick Q: do we need a separate pseudonymization example vs redaction? I'm leaning toward showing both, with clear guidance on when to use each (legal vs operational). :thinking_face:

liam (legal): Agreed on both. Suggest wording: "retain minimal identifiers only for investigatory timelines; pseudonymize where analytics require continuity; redact for deletion requests and regulatory holds." I'll draft a short blurb for the playbook.

maya (eng-docs): I can add SDK snippets (py/ts/ruby) showing pseudonymize() + redact() helpers. Can someone confirm the recommended TTL values to surface in examples?

jordan (docs): Thinking we surface three tiers: short (7–30 days), medium (90–180 days), long (2–7 years) with examples of what falls in each. We should mark them as "example values — consult legal/security for final numbers."

emma (security): That works. For SOC2-language, prefer: "retention period established according to business need and legal obligations; records are periodically reviewed and disposed of per policy." Avoid words like "indefinitely".

liam (legal): I'll provide two sample sentences for the top-level policy and one for the customer-facing FAQ. Will post as a comment on the PR.

maya (eng-docs): Drafted code snippets — small function shown inline. Feedback welcome.

maya (eng-docs): ```python
# pseudonymize example
def pseudonymize(record):
    # replace user id with stable hash
    record['user_id'] = hash(record['user_id'])[:16]
    return record

# redact example
def redact(record, fields=('email','ssn')):
    for f in fields:
        record[f] = None
    return record
```

emma (security): Nice. Can you add a note about deterministic vs non-deterministic pseudonyms (i.e., salted hashing for re-identification risk)? Also call out that hashing alone is not sufficient for high-risk PII.

maya (eng-docs): On it. I'll add a short paragraph and a TS snippet that uses a KMS-backed salt.

devbot: PR #4923 status: changes requested by emma (security).

jordan (docs): Two other asks: 1) add a short migration guide for teams that currently store raw audit logs (how to roll forward with a redaction pass + backfill plan) and 2) ensure links to the KMS/infrastructure pages are correct (we had a dead link last week).

liam (legal): For the migration guide, recommend an append-only epoch approach — keep original logs in a restricted archive for X days while backfilling pseudonymized versions into active storage. I'll add legal constraints and hold language.

emma (security): +1. Also add a checklist for reviewers: (a) confirm sample TTL values are appropriate for use-case, (b) verify SDK snippets call our vetted crypto libs, (c) ensure customer-facing wording avoids operational detail.

maya (eng-docs): I'll add the checklist and do a link sweep. Can someone ping infra to confirm the KMS doc url?
